name: SOMA
oneLiner: An AI fitness and nutrition coach for iPhone: two agents read the health data already on the phone and return one plan a day — the session, the food, and the reason behind both.
sourceOfTruth: soma-landing/public/pricing.md — the machine-readable brief the marketing site publishes. Re-read it before quoting a price or a feature; it carries a 'Last updated' date and this copy will drift.
platform: iPhone, iOS 17+. Android on the roadmap.
status: invite-only beta; waitlist open at https://soma4health.com/#waitlist

io.input: the wearables and sensors the person already owns
io.output: one adaptive daily plan — workout + macros — and the reasoning behind it

audience.core: People who already track their health on a watch or ring and still do not know what to do on a given day. They own the data; nobody turns it into a decision.
types: Multi-device owners — Apple Watch plus Oura or Whoop, with the numbers spread across apps that do not talk to each other
Women training seriously around a real life — work, cycle, sleep debt — for whom a fixed programme breaks the first bad week
Returners — people restarting after a pause who need the plan to meet the body they have today, not the one they had
Beginners who bought the watch and never got past the rings
lessSuitable: people who want a human coach relationship
athletes on a periodised programme from a real coach
anyone expecting a medical or diagnostic tool
Android users, until the app ships there

features.name: One adaptive daily plan
features.what: workout and macros for today, rebuilt from last night's sleep and recent strain

features.name: Gym scan
features.what: photograph any room; the session rebuilds around the equipment actually there

features.name: Progress compare
features.what: goal photo against current photo, side by side

features.name: Recipe generation
features.what: meals from what is in the fridge, sized to the calories and macros left today

features.name: Wearable integrations
features.what: Apple Health as the hub, plus Apple Watch, Oura, Whoop. Garmin, Fitbit, Polar, Samsung Health, Withings, Strava in progress.

differentiators: Vendor-independent: reasons across devices instead of locking the person into one brand's app
No new hardware — it reads the sensors already owned
Returns a decision, not a dashboard: what to do today and why
Adapts daily: a bad night changes the session rather than breaking the plan

plans.name: Membership, yearly
plans.note: $13.33/mo equivalent; 3-day free trial exists on this plan only

plans.name: Waitlist
plans.note: The Data-Backed Reset Guide, field notes, first access at launch

notPurchasable: A second tier (deeper health reports, biomarker/bloodwork integration, cycle-synced programming) is indicated at $79.99/month and is NOT on sale. Never present it as available.

is: calm — the product is the opposite of hustle content
avoid: any medical or diagnostic claim — SOMA is not a medical device, does not diagnose, treat, or replace a clinician
body-scan-from-a-photo claims: the research sheet is full of them and the app does not do it. Progress compare puts two photos side by side; it does not read body composition from an image.
weight-loss guarantees, timelines, or numbers ('lose 5kg in 4 weeks')
'replaces your trainer' as a factual claim — a comparison of speed is fine, a claim of equivalence is not
hormone, cycle or bloodwork features — that tier is not on sale
shaming, before/after moralising, or 'nothing tastes as good as' register

compliance: Health claims are the risk surface of this account. If a line implies a medical outcome, cut it. Prices drift — verify against soma-landing/public/pricing.md before publishing any figure.
